9 Best Things to Do in Marrakesh 🕌✨ 1) Stay in a Riad 🛏️  feel the authentic Moroccan vibe, from the mosaic tiles to the whisper-quiet courtyards. Riads offer privacy, fewer crowds, and a home-away-from-home feel with traditional decor, often a peaceful rooftop terrace, and staff who treat you like family. Perfect for a truly Moroccan experience without the hotel hustle. 2) Best Coffee at Bacha Coffee ☕️✨ (Location: https://goo.gl/maps/6u3Xx9J9xqv1w9Qw7) Silky espresso, perfectly balanced blends, and a chic, relaxed atmosphere. Great latte art, friendly baristas, and a bright, stylish space to post your vibes. Pro tip: try their signature crush coffee and pastry pairing. 3) Explore the Souks 🧿🌀 Fun tip: haggle with a smile, never agree to the first price! Make it a playful game, sample spices, and test your bargaining skills. Lose yourself in ribbons of color, leather, pottery, and lamps. The thrill of the find is half the fun! 4) Visit Ben Youssef Madrasa 🕌 A jaw-dropping historic site with intricate tilework, carved wood, and serene courtyards. It’s a perfect spot for photos that scream old-world Marrakech charm. 5) Jardin Majorelle 🌿💙 iconic cobalt-blue paths, lush botanical displays, and a peaceful escape from the market buzz. A must-see for color lovers and plant enthusiasts, plus it’s connected to the Yves Saint Laurent legacy. 6) Ourika Valley Day Trip 🚙🌄 about 1 hour from central Marrakech (depending on traffic). What to expect: stunning valley scenery, Berber villages, waterfalls, and a cooler climate. A refreshing break from the medina with photo-worthy viewpoints. 7) Agafay Desert Experience 🐫🏜️ Highlights: camel ride under the open sky, squad  bike moments, and magical desert views. Luxe touch: stay at a desert camp with plush lounges, gourmet meals, and starlit dinners. Perfect for a memorable  outing. 8) Dinner at La Trattoria 🍝🇮🇹  warm, cozy ambiance with authentic Italian flavors in Marrakech. Great for a relaxed evening, fresh pastas, and a lively dining vibe after a day of exploration. 9) Jemaa el-Fnaa - The Heart of Marrakech 🎭💃 Do it for the vibes: bustling square, street performances, snake charmers, and a feast for the senses. Pro tip: bring some cash for photos with performers and for quick bites. Best times: late afternoon into evening when the energy peaks. #Marrakesh #Morocco #TravelTikTok #Riads #Souks

videos.caption: Moroccon history edit 🇲🇦☀️ | Song: Baixo Cristal Teclas Morocco, officially the Kingdom of Morocco, is a country located in the northwest corner of Africa. It borders the Atlantic Ocean, the Mediterranean Sea, Algeria, and Western Sahara, making it one of the most strategically located nations on the continent. Its unique position has allowed it to serve as a bridge between Africa, Europe, and the Middle East for thousands of years. Morocco has one of the richest histories in Africa. It was home to the Amazigh (Berber) peoples long before the arrival of Islam in the 7th century. Over the centuries, powerful dynasties such as the Almoravids, Almohads, Saadians, and Alaouites transformed Morocco into one of the strongest states in North Africa. At their height, Moroccan empires ruled territories stretching into modern-day Algeria, Mauritania, Mali, and southern Spain. The country also remained independent from the Ottoman Empire and successfully defended itself against several European invasions. Today, Morocco is known for its diverse landscapes, from the snowy Atlas Mountains to the vast Sahara Desert and its long Atlantic and Mediterranean coastlines. Its cities, including Rabat, Casablanca, Marrakesh, and Fez, are famous for their historic architecture, colorful markets, and rich cultural traditions. Moroccan culture blends Amazigh, Arab, Andalusian, African, and European influences. The country is renowned for its cuisine, traditional craftsmanship, music, and hospitality. Dishes such as tagine and couscous are enjoyed worldwide, while Moroccan mint tea has become a symbol of welcoming guests. In recent decades, Morocco has developed one of Africa's largest economies, with strengths in tourism, agriculture, automotive manufacturing, renewable energy, and phosphate production. The country also gained worldwide recognition when its national football team became the first African nation to reach the FIFA World Cup semifinals in 2022. With over a thousand years of continuous statehood, a rich imperial history, diverse landscapes, and a unique blend of cultures, Morocco remains one of Africa's most influential and historically significant countries. #FYP #Morocco #History #FY #creatorsearchinsights  @🇱🇰✝️ 𝓛𝓪𝓷𝓴𝓪𝓷✝️🇱🇰 (tournament)

5 things to know before going to Marrakech👇🇲🇦 1️⃣ Moroccan taxis WILL overcharge you, download @inDrive before you arrive. It works at the airport, you set your own price, so there’s no negotiation needed 🚖  2️⃣ Be aware of the animal abuse at Jemaa el-Fnaa. Men walk the square with monkeys in chains and snakes with their teeth removed, don’t pay if they confront you 🙊  3️⃣ Where you stay matters. I found my riad on the @cozycozy app, which compared the prices across all the major booking sites. Agoda was £40 vs £45 on Booking.com, saving £35 over 7 nights 🏨  4️⃣ Eat all the street food. Vendors need licences, so it’s clean, fresh and cheap. I reccoemnd trying this sardine salad just off the main square, search “fried fish” on google maps 🍗  5️⃣ Stay safe in the medina. Before giving your opinion about Morocco, you should obviously do a little research first. Step one: open a book about Moroccan history. Yes, an actual book with pages, because apparently watching a few TikToks is not enough to become an expert on an entire country. Start by learning about the Amazigh people, whose presence in North Africa goes back thousands of years. Learn about the different Amazigh communities in Morocco, their historical regions, languages, cultures, and traditions. You can look into groups such as the Rifains in the Rif, the Chleuhs in the Souss and southern regions, Amazigh communities of the Middle Atlas, and many others throughout the country. Because, surprisingly, “Amazigh” does not describe one single identical population living in one exact place. Then study Moroccan history before the Arab and Islamic periods: ancient North African populations, Phoenician and Carthaginian influences, the Roman period, and the different dynasties and political changes that shaped Morocco over time. After that, learn about the spread of Arabic language and culture, as well as the migrations, exchanges, and mixing of populations that happened throughout North African history. Then comes everyone’s favorite part: genetics. This is where you should actually read scientific studies instead of looking at one DNA chart on TikTok and suddenly deciding that you have discovered the complete genetic history of an entire population. Moroccan populations have a complex genetic history, with a major ancient North African component alongside influences from different populations that moved through and interacted with North Africa throughout history. Results can also vary between regions and populations, so maybe don’t take one study about one specific group and use it as the universal answer for every Moroccan. You should also learn the difference between ancestry, culture, language, identity, and genetics, because they are not the same thing. Speaking Arabic does not automatically mean having exactly the same genetic ancestry as every other Arabic-speaking person, just as being Amazigh does not mean belonging to one genetically identical population. Human history is, unfortunately for anyone looking for an easy answer, a little more complicated than a “choose your ethnicity” quiz. Then research Amazigh languages in Morocco, their history and official status, as well as the cultural diversity between different Moroccan regions. Learn how Amazigh, Arab, Moroccan, regional, and family identities can sometimes overlap rather than simply cancel each other out. Finally, after studying all of that, you might actually be ready to talk about Morocco without reducing thousands of years of history to two sentences you found online. If you genuinely want to understand Moroccan origins, you have to look at history, archaeology, languages, migrations, culture, and genetics together. There you go. You can officially begin your studies on Morocco now. Good luck with the curriculum. It’s slightly more complicated than expected. #morocco#aespa#ningning#ⵣ🇲🇦 #aespa
